note: The spine. Every provider Record Atlas can point at, with what it actually costs to look. `access` is the map's colour and must describe the ordinary visitor's experience, not the best case: FamilySearch is `account` because its images need a free login and some are locked to a Family History Centre. Every row carries `checked`; a row nobody has re-checked in a year should be treated as a claim, not a fact. `at` is where the paper is, or where the portal is run from, at CITY level — a street pin implies a precision that does not survive an institution moving building. A provider with no `at` has no single home: an aggregator, a commercial subscription, or a volunteer index that lives on a server.

providers.name: ANNO — Austrian Newspapers Online
providers.what: The Austrian National Library's digitised newspaper run. Full-text searchable, and it covers the whole empire — which is why it finds Croatian and Istrian names.

providers.name: ARHiNET — Croatian State Archives
providers.what: The Croatian State Archives, and through it the national register of archival fonds — which archive holds which fonds; the paper itself is almost all unphotographed. THE OLD LINK HERE WAS DEAD. This row pointed at arhinet.arhiv.hr, which no longer resolves at all — NXDOMAIN on Google's and Cloudflare's resolvers both, not a timeout or a redirect, so every Croatian researcher who clicked ARHiNET on this map got nothing. The successor is HAIS at hais.arhiv.hr, which resolves to 161.53.80.20 and did not answer this project's requests at all; unable to tell a service that is down from one that does not answer us, this points at the archive's own site, which does answer, rather than shipping a second link nobody can open.

providers.name: Acta Publica
providers.what: Moravian and Silesian parish registers, free. The Czech regional archives each publish their own; this is the Brno one.

providers.name: Ancestry
providers.what: The largest commercial collection. Strong on the English-speaking world, censuses and immigration; weak on continental parish registers.

providers.name: Antenati
providers.what: The Italian state archives' own portal. Civil registration images from 1806, free and without an account — the best national genealogy portal in Europe.

providers.name: Archion
providers.what: The German Protestant church archives' own portal. Subscription by the month; the only route to many Lutheran registers.

providers.name: Archives New Zealand — Collections
providers.what: New Zealand probate, military and immigration records, much of it digitised and free.

providers.name: Archives d'Alsace — Bas-Rhin
providers.what: Strasbourg. Registers free online, and written in whichever language the ground belonged to that decade — French to 1871, German to 1918, French again, German again from 1940.

providers.name: Archives d'Alsace — Haut-Rhin
providers.what: Colmar. The southern half of Alsace, with the same language flips and the same free access.

providers.name: Archives départementales de la Moselle
providers.what: Metz. Moselle went with Alsace in 1871 and came back with it in 1918, which is why a Lorraine family's records can be in German for forty-seven years and French on either side.

providers.name: Archivo General de la Nación (Argentina)
providers.what: Argentina's national archive — immigration and naturalisation above all. Civil registration itself is PROVINCIAL and is not here; the provinces keep their own.

providers.name: Archiwum Główne Akt Dawnych (AGAD)
providers.what: Warsaw's archive of the old Republic — the metrical books of the Polish partitions, including eastern Galician parishes now in Ukraine. Catalogued here; the scans are published through Szukaj w Archiwach.

providers.name: Arhiv Bosne i Hercegovine
providers.what: The state archive in Sarajevo. Ottoman-era defters, the Austro-Hungarian administration's own paper from 1878, and almost nothing online — this is a letter or a visit.

providers.name: Arhiv Republike Slovenije
providers.what: Ljubljana. The Slovenian state archive — the Habsburg land records for Carniola, the Franciscean cadastre, and the finding aids that SIRAnet searches. Its own arhiv.gov.si serves http only, so the entry here points at the state portal page, which does not.

providers.name: Arhiv Srbije
providers.what: The Serbian state archive. Church registers for the pre-1918 Kingdom, and the administrative record of a state that was Ottoman ground until 1878.

providers.name: Arhiv Vojvodine
providers.what: Novi Sad. Vojvodina was Hungarian ground until 1918, so its registers are in the Hungarian series and its finding aids are in three languages — this archive is where the two filing systems meet.

providers.name: Arhivele Naționale ale României
providers.what: The Romanian national archives, county by county. Holds the Bukovinan and Transylvanian registers for the years those provinces were Romanian, which is not the same span as the years they existed.

providers.name: Arolsen Archives
providers.what: The former International Tracing Service. Concentration camp, forced labour and displaced-persons records for some seventeen and a half million people, free and fully indexed.

providers.name: BAnQ numérique — Bibliothèque et Archives nationales du Québec
providers.what: Quebec's civil-registration registers — the parish registers that WERE the civil registration, kept in duplicate from 1621 and among the most complete continuous records anywhere in the Americas. Free.

providers.name: BeWeB — Beni ecclesiastici in web
providers.what: The Italian Church's own register of what its dioceses and parishes hold. It does not show you the books — it tells you which diocesan archive to write to for a parish register, which for pre-1809 southern Italy is the only route there is.

providers.name: BillionGraves
providers.what: GPS-tagged headstone photographs. Smaller than Find a Grave but its coordinates are per-stone, which Find a Grave's often are not.

providers.name: Bundesarchiv
providers.what: The German Federal Archives. Civil and military administration of the Prussian provinces, the wartime records, and the card indexes of the expelled — much of it for ground that is no longer German.

providers.name: Chronicling America
providers.what: The Library of Congress's digitised American newspapers, full-text and free.

providers.name: Delpher
providers.what: Dutch newspapers, books and periodicals, full-text and free. Death notices here fill gaps the registers leave.

providers.name: Digitalarkivet
providers.what: The Norwegian National Archives, free and largely indexed — censuses, parish registers, emigration lists.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Pazinu
providers.what: The Pazin State Archive, which holds the parish registers of central Istria. They will search, certify and post a named record for a fee.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Rijeci
providers.what: The Rijeka State Archive — the Kvarner, Fiume's corpus separatum administration, and the Liburnian coast.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Zadru
providers.what: The Zadar State Archive, which holds the Venetian and Austrian registers of Dalmatia — including parishes whose books never went to Split.

providers.name: FamilySearch
providers.what: The largest free collection of record images and indexes in the world. A free account is required, and a minority of images are restricted to Family History Centres and affiliate libraries.

providers.name: Find a Grave
providers.what: Volunteer-photographed headstones and cemetery indexes, worldwide, with very uneven coverage. Owned by Ancestry but free to read.

providers.name: Findmypast
providers.what: Commercial. The strongest British and Irish collection, including parish registers licensed from diocesan archives and the 1921 census of England and Wales.

providers.name: FreeBMD / FreeREG / FreeCEN
providers.what: Volunteer transcriptions of English and Welsh civil registration, parish registers and censuses. Free, an index only, and not complete.

providers.name: GenTeam.at
providers.what: Volunteer indexes to the Habsburg lands — Vienna's parish registers, Jewish records, school and guild lists. Free with an account, and it reaches ground the church portals do not.

providers.name: Geneanet
providers.what: Member-contributed trees and transcriptions, strongest in France. Much is free; a Premium tier gates some search and images.

providers.name: General Register Office (England and Wales)
providers.what: The official index to English and Welsh civil registration from 1837. The index is a reference, not a record — you order the certificate, and it is charged.

providers.name: Geneteka
providers.what: A volunteer index of Polish parish registers, by surname and parish. An index only — it points you at the scan rather than showing it. — NOTE: the service was answering HTTP 500 on 16 September 2026. Its parent society, genealodzy.pl, is up; the index may be back by the time you read this.

providers.name: Geni
providers.what: One shared world tree. Useful for finding other researchers on the same line; not a record source, and its assertions are only as good as their citations.

providers.name: Généalogie Québec / the Drouin Collection
providers.what: The Drouin microfilms indexed — Quebec and francophone North America, including the Acadian and New England parishes the deportations and the mill towns scattered people into.

providers.name: Hrčak
providers.what: The portal of Croatian scientific journals, free and full-text. Local history articles here routinely name and date ordinary families.

providers.name: Hungaricana
providers.what: The Hungarian cultural heritage portal — maps, censuses, urbaria and archival finding aids for the whole Kingdom of Hungary, not today's borders.

providers.name: Internet Archive
providers.what: Full-text search across millions of digitised books, including parish histories, nobiliaries and local monographs that name ordinary people.

providers.name: IrishGenealogy.ie
providers.what: Irish civil registration images and church records, free and without an account. The single best free national source in these islands.

holdings.note: Index and register images. The open window rolls forward each 1 January under the 100-year rule.
Non-Catholic marriages from 1845, all marriages from 1864. Images under the 75-year rule.

holdings.what: Roman Catholic parish registers — Dublin, Kerry, Cork & Ross, Carlow
holdings.note: Baptisms, marriages and burials for these dioceses only. The rest of the country is at the National Library's register microfilms.

holdings.what: Church of Ireland registers — Dublin, Kerry, Carlow
holdings.note: A small survival. Most Church of Ireland registers burned in the Four Courts in 1922.

holdings.what: Presbyterian registers — a small number of congregations

providers.holdingsNote: RECORDED, NOT HARVESTED, and that is a weaker claim. irishgenealogy.ie sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that answers 403 to anything but a human's browser, so this list is written from the site's own published description of what it holds rather than read off the page. Treat the diocesan coverage as the shape of the thing and check the live page before relying on a specific year. See data/_declined.json for why it was not scraped.

providers.name: JewishGen
providers.what: The central Jewish genealogy resource — town-level KehilaLinks, burial and Holocaust databases, and revision lists for eastern Europe.

providers.name: Kansallisarkisto / HisKi
providers.what: The Finnish National Archives, plus the Genealogical Society's HisKi parish transcriptions. Free.

providers.name: Library and Archives Canada
providers.what: Canadian censuses, immigration and military service records, free.

providers.name: Lietuvos archyvai (Lithuanian State Archives)
providers.what: The Lithuanian state archives, including the Memel/Klaipėda district — German ground until 1945 whose records did not all leave with the population.

providers.name: Magyar Nemzeti Levéltár (Hungarian National Archives)
providers.what: The archives of the Kingdom of Hungary, which until 1920 meant Slovakia, Transylvania, the Banat and Croatia as well. Civil registration duplicates from 1895 are here even where the ground is now in another country.

providers.name: Matricula Online
providers.what: Diocesan parish registers photographed and served free, without an account. Austria and much of Germany and Poland; the Italian entries are South Tyrol.

providers.name: MyHeritage
providers.what: Commercial, with a large tree network and good European newspaper and directory coverage. Search is free; opening a record is not.

providers.name: NAAIRS — National Archives of South Africa
providers.what: The South African archives index — estate files above all, which are the backbone of South African genealogy. An index; the file is ordered from the depot.

providers.name: National Archives Catalog (NARA)
providers.what: The US National Archives catalogue and scans — naturalisations, passenger lists, military service, land.

providers.name: National Archives of Australia — RecordSearch
providers.what: Immigration and naturalisation files, service records and alien registration — including the wartime files of European arrivals.

providers.name: National Archives of Ireland
providers.what: What survived 1922 and what was rebuilt since — the 1901 and 1911 censuses in full and free, Tithe Applotment books, wills and the census fragments recovered from other collections.

providers.name: National Library of Ireland — Catholic Parish Registers
providers.what: Every surviving Irish Catholic parish register to 1880, photographed and free. Browse only — no index.

providers.name: National Records of Scotland
providers.what: The archive behind ScotlandsPeople. Kirk session records, sasines, services of heirs and the estate papers — the Scottish sources that are not births, marriages and deaths.

providers.name: PARES
providers.what: The Spanish archives portal — strongest on emigration to the Americas and on military and colonial service.

providers.name: PRONI — Public Record Office of Northern Ireland
providers.what: The record office for the six counties, and the reason Ulster research is not as badly burnt as the rest of Ireland: PRONI held copies and estate papers that were never in the Four Courts. Church records, wills, valuation revision books.

providers.name: Porta fontium
providers.what: A Bavarian–Czech joint portal. Parish registers of western Bohemia, free.

providers.name: Queensland Historical BDM Index
providers.what: Queensland's historical births, deaths and marriages index. Free to search; certificates are charged. Every Australian state runs its own.

providers.name: Raduraksti — Latvian State Historical Archives
providers.what: Latvia's church registers, revision lists and the 1935 census, scanned. A free account, and the Baltic German Lutheran registers of Livonia and Courland are the bulk of it.

providers.name: Rigsarkivet — Arkivalieronline
providers.what: The Danish National Archives. Parish registers and censuses, free.

providers.name: Riksarkivet — Digitala forskarsalen
providers.what: The Swedish National Archives. Much is now free; the highest-quality parish register images are on the commercial ArkivDigital.

providers.name: SIRAnet
providers.what: The Slovenian regional archives' shared catalogue. Largely a finding aid — it tells you the book exists and where it is.

providers.name: Saaga — Estonian National Archives
providers.what: Estonia's parish registers, revision lists and soul lists, photographed and free. Lutheran registers in German, Orthodox in Russian, and the 19th-century revision lists that name a whole household at once.

providers.name: ScotlandsPeople
providers.what: The official Scottish records — statutory registers, old parish registers, censuses and wills. Pay-per-view credits, and the only lawful route to most of it.

providers.name: Statue of Liberty–Ellis Island Foundation
providers.what: Passenger arrivals at New York, 1820–1957, with manifest images. Free with an account.

providers.name: Szukaj w Archiwach
providers.what: The Polish state archives' scans, free and without an account. Covers ground now in Ukraine, Belarus and Lithuania as well as Poland.

providers.name: The National Archives — Discovery
providers.what: The catalogue of the UK National Archives and some 2,500 other British archives. The catalogue is free; downloads are often charged.

providers.name: Torre do Tombo / Digitarq
providers.what: The Portuguese national archive's scans, free. District archives publish parish registers through the same system.

providers.name: Trove
providers.what: The National Library of Australia's newspaper archive. Free, full-text, and the single best source for Australian family detail before 1955.

providers.name: WieWasWie / Open Archieven
providers.what: The Dutch civil registration indexes, pooled from every regional archive. Free, and unusually complete.

providers.name: WikiTree
providers.what: A free, single shared tree with an unusually strong sourcing culture. Not a record source.

providers.name: Yad Vashem — Central Database of Shoah Victims' Names
providers.what: Names and testimony pages for victims of the Shoah, free.

providers.name: dLib.si
providers.what: The Digital Library of Slovenia. Newspapers, journals and books, full-text searchable — and it reaches Istrian and Littoral material.

providers.name: eGGSA — Genealogical Society of South Africa
providers.what: Volunteer photographs of South African gravestones and transcriptions of Dutch Reformed Church registers and newspaper notices. Free, and for the Cape before 1895 it is often the only index there is.

providers.name: DZS — Names and surnames in the Republic of Croatia
providers.what: The Croatian Bureau of Statistics' own lookup: how many people carried a given surname at the 2011 census, with a confidentiality floor of 10. One name at a time — there is no list of what exists, so it answers a question you bring rather than handing over a table. Croatia's PxWeb API has no surname data at all, which is why this atlas missed it for a week.

providers.name: Acta Croatica
providers.what: Croatian historical documents indexed by the people named in them, plus a page per surname giving its spelling variants, the towns it is thickest in, and where its bearers emigrated. The closest thing anywhere to what this atlas does, done for names instead of places. Its figures are derived and carry no stated licence, so this is a link, not a source of rows.

providers.name: Indeks — Hrvatsko rodoslovno društvo
providers.what: A Croatian genealogical index, run by the genealogical society. Its robots.txt names this class of agent and refuses it, so this atlas links to it and does not read it — see data/_declined.json.
